entries.title: II Chronicles 36:1
segments: When wise and pious rulers are removed and are succeeded by those who are foolish and wicked, it is a punishment of the people for their sins; and where it does not produce reformation, it forebodes approaching destruction.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:6
segments: To carry him to Babylon; either Nebuchadnezzar did not carry out his purpose of transporting Jehoiakim to Babylon, or he restored him again to Jerusalem, and permitted him to reign there as his tributary. See

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:7
segments: God sometimes suffers the wicked to obtain great power, that they may be scourges of his people on account of their sins.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:9
segments: , he is said to have been eighteen years old.  This latter is generally thought to be the true reading.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:12
segments: No trials, without the grace of God, will humble and purify the human heart, or lead men to forsake their sins and turn to the Lord.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:13
segments: Made him swear; swear allegiance to the king of Babylon.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:16
segments: When men mock the messengers whom God sends to reclaim them, and despise their words or mercy and love, they are ripening for wrath against which there will be no remedy.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:20
segments: Until the reign of the kingdom of Persia; about seventy years.

entries.title: II Chronicles 36:21
segments: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths; the sabbatical year occurred every seventh year.

In four hundred and ninety years there would be seventy sabbatical years.  It has been supposed that the observance of the sabbatical year had been omitted for about that space of time before the Babylonish captivity; that is, from about the time of the establishment of the monarchy. 
 
The providence of God manifests the truth of his word; and shows that when a declaration has once gone out of his mouth, it will in due time be accomplished.
